intent.title: Korean support (i18n)
intent.request:
I'd like to write a new intent for i18n (Korean support). Is this correct to call it a new intent? Or should I call it a new issue?

Create new intent
intent.problem: Every gate view is in English only. The human deciding at the gates is a native Korean speaker who works in English, so each decision is made through a second language, and a label or status line that is misread can lead to approving the wrong thing. The tool has no way to present its views in another language.
acceptance: A gate view rendered in Korean shows every fixed label, badge, button, and status line in Korean.
A gate view rendered without choosing a language is unchanged from today.
Authored text (the request, problem, criteria, questions, and answers) appears exactly as written in every language.
An approval sent from a Korean view names the same gate and rev, and is accepted the same way, as one sent from an English view.
Adding another language takes only a new set of translations, with no change to any view (Q2).
The language is each person's own choice: one person choosing a language never changes what anyone else sees (Q3).
A person's language choice applies in every repo they work in, without setting it per repo (Q5).
When a request is written in Korean, the agent-written fields of its intent and plan are in Korean too (Q4).

deferred.item: Per-viewer language in the team phase's coordinator views, read from the viewer's identity
deferred.reason: Viewer identity exists only in the team phase (Q5).

nonGoals.reason: Every interpretation is checked against the human's own words; a translated request or answer would no longer be those words.

nonGoals.item: Translating the CLI's messages and errors
nonGoals.reason: Agents read CLI output and fix against its errors; the human decides in the gate views (Q1).

decisions.question: What does Korean support cover: only the rendered gate views, or also the CLI's messages and errors?
decisions.answer: Gate views only (Recommended): labels, badges, buttons, and status lines in rendered views. CLI messages and errors stay English.

decisions.question: Is this Korean only, or a general mechanism where Korean is the first added language?
decisions.answer: General, en + ko (Recommended): views read their text from a per-language set of translations; another language is added as a new set, with no view changes.

decisions.question: How is the language chosen for a view?
decisions.answer: It should be a personal setting. But not sure the best way to ensure it.

decisions.question: Where does the personal language setting live, and how far does it reach?
decisions.answer: User-level, all repos (Recommended): stored with the person like their git name and email (user-level git config), never in a repo. Team-phase views read it from the viewer's identity, deferred to #4.

decisions.question: When the human writes a request in Korean, what language do agents write the rest of the intent and plan in?
decisions.answer: The request's language (Recommended): a Korean request gets a Korean problem, criteria, questions, and steps.

decisions.question: Each gate button sends a fixed chat message that the agent acts on, such as "Approve the intent gate for #8 at rev e28140a." In a Korean view, is that message Korean or English?
decisions.answer: Korean message: in a Korean view the whole button is Korean, including the message it sends. The approval rule and skills recognize a Korean approval that names the gate and the rev.

steps.summary: Views read every fixed text from an English catalog passed in by language
steps.riskReason: Touches every renderer; a string left inline or mistyped changes the English views everyone sees today.

add.type: every fixed label, heading, note, pill, button label, and button message the views show
a language code with a catalog

change.to: (title, fragment, lang = 'en'), and <html lang> follows it

rules.text: no view has an English word inline; step kinds, symbols, revs, and IDs stay as they are, since they're identifiers
counts and lists in text come from catalog functions, so a language can phrase plurals and word order its own way

invariants.text: every view rendered without a language is byte-identical to before

evidence: golden files captured before the change from the samples and #1-#8's views, compared after it

steps.summary: A Korean catalog, including the messages buttons send
steps.riskReason: Adds a catalog nothing selects until the CLI reads the personal setting.

rules.text: CATALOGS has en and ko, and every catalog has exactly en's keys
a view rendered in ko contains none of en's fixed strings
a ko button message names the same intent, gate, and rev as the en one (Q6)
authored text renders exactly as stored in ko and en

evidence: the #8 intent gate and a sample result gate rendered in ko, read by the human

steps.summary: render reads the person's language from their user-level git config
steps.riskReason: Without the setting, render behaves exactly as today.

add.signature: (): Lang, from git config --global ldd.lang, 'en' when unset

rules.text: render passes personalLang() to every format, and the loader format embeds it in the call it emits
an ldd.lang with no catalog fails with the list of languages, rather than falling back to English
only the user-level config is read; a repo's own config never sets the language (Q5)
the usage text says how to set it: git config --global ldd.lang ko

evidence: test/i18n.test.ts runs the CLI with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointed at a temporary file

steps.summary: Skills write in the request's language and accept an approval in any language
steps.riskReason: The approval rule guards the gates; widening it to Korean must still require the gate and the rev.

rules.text: agents write every authored field of an intent and its plan in the request's language (Q4)
an approval counts in any language when it explicitly says to approve and names the gate and the rev, as the buttons in every language do (Q6)

evidence: dry run: structure a short Korean request with the skill; its fields come out in Korean and intent-view validates it

steps.summary: Record #8's decisions in the design record
evidence: the human reads languages.md against Q1-Q6
